summary: Both editions were reviewed independently against all thirteen paragraphs of the selected working Greek. No concrete fidelity defect was identified. Both preserve the servant/Son identification, the selected negative in VI.1, the universal inability-to-understand assertion, the creator-Spirit and flesh-partnership language, and the reward statement with its stated qualifications. Reader-facing servant terminology follows current policy. The notes distinguish conjectures and restorations from preserved text, disclose substantive alternatives, and accurately reflect the supplied bounded comparison reports without treating physical losses as evidence for omission. Acceptance concerns fidelity to this working source and the supplied reports; it does not authenticate unseen images, certify the cited editions, establish a unique interpretation, or constitute exhaustive manuscript collation.
